age_bmi_rise.why: Older and heavier people get a steeply higher predicted risk once both pass a threshold, and the age-by-bmi probe reproduces it (bmi 34 vs 22 at age 60: 97% vs 32%).

young_female_lowering.why: Women and young people get a lower predicted risk with a sex gap that closes by about 70, confirmed by the age-by-sex probe and by women being lower on 19,803 of 24,000 rows.

young_uninsured_lowering.why: The probe confirms what it does (lowers risk for the uninsured below old age and the young insured), but the hypothesis itself says this has no domain reading.

score_rural_rise.why: High score raising risk earlier for rural people holds, but the unit is gated just as strongly by low bmi (and also by higher income), which has no reading and makes thin, high-score people much riskier.

income_low_score_lowering.why: As a part it lowers risk for higher incomes, more at low scores, as the income-by-score probe shows; only the whole-model extension of that reading fails (V17).

visits_smoker_rise.why: Several visits raise the risk with smokers crossing the threshold at fewer visits (3 visits: 58% smoker vs 31% non-smoker), as the probe shows.
